Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to promoting cultural tourism, preserving historical heritage and supporting initiatives that would always showcase the state’s tourism potential. He stated this at the 2026 Oronna Ilaro Festival, according to a statement made available to PUNCH Online on Sunday. The event was themed ‘Festival of Dawn of New Glory.’ Represented by the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism, Sesan Fagbayi, the governor stated that the event’s theme is a call for collective responsibility, purposeful leadership and renewed commitment to preserving the values and traditions that define the people. Abiodun said that the theme underscored the need to “translate shared history and cultural pride into meaningful actions that promote unity, economic advancement, youth empowerment and sustainable community development.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He said his administration is committed to promoting cultural tourism, preserving historical heritage and creating opportunities for the “state’s rich cultural heritage to contribute meaningfully to economic growth, employment generation and overall development of the state.” The governor also commended the Olu of Ilaro and Paramount Ruler of Yewaland, Oba Kehinde Olugbenle, the Council of Chiefs, festival organisers and other stakeholders for sustaining the important cultural celebration. He urged the sons and daughters of Yewaland to “embrace the spirit of the festival by promoting culture, tourism, unity, peace, mutual understanding and collective action towards projecting the heritage of Yewaland for the benefit of present and future generations. Lions Clubs screen over 200 Ogun residents for diabetes Trade ministry cracks down on cheating measures in Ogun Abiodun demands arrest of Odegbami’s attackers “He also called on the people to continue supporting initiatives that preserve historical heritage and create opportunities for cultural traditions to drive economic growth, generate employment and contribute to the overall development of the state.” In his welcome address, the Chairman of the 2026 Oronna Ilaro Festival Committee, Lekan Asunni, said this year’s theme captured the aspirations of the Ilaro people for renewed hope, cultural renaissance, unity and sustainable development. “He emphasised the importance of youth engagement in sustaining cultural identity and promoting community development, noting that greater involvement of young people was critical to preventing the gradual extinction of customs and traditions handed down by previous generations. “In his address, the Olu of Ilaro and Paramount Ruler of Yewaland, Oba (Dr.) Olugbenle, welcomed guests and appreciated the Abiodun-led administration for its unwavering commitment to promoting and preserving the state’s cultural heritage. “The monarch stressed the importance of intergenerational collaboration in cultural preservation, urging the older generation to continually involve young people in traditional practices and customs to prevent them from going extinct,” the statement read.
